overview: This is the northern stretch of Perran Beach, known as Perran Sands: the wilder end of the huge, two-mile beach that sweeps up from Perranporth towards Ligger Point. Behind it lie the vast dunes of Penhale Sands.

It has a long history. St Piran, Cornwall’s patron saint, is said to have founded an oratory in the dunes here in the 7th century; it lay buried under the sand for centuries before being uncovered in 1835. Iron ore was once mined from a vein on the beach, too.

expect.title: Space
expect.text: Walk north away from the town end and you’ll find plenty of room even in summer.

expect.title: Penhale Sands
expect.text: Huge dunes behind the beach, where St Piran’s Oratory was rediscovered.

expect.title: Surf
expect.text: Like the rest of Perran Beach, it faces west into the Atlantic and picks up surf.

goodToKnow.label: Where it is
goodToKnow.text: Around 7 miles south-west of Newquay, at the northern end of Perranporth’s beach.

week.text: Great for a long beach walk or a quieter spot than the busy Perranporth end. It faces west, so evenings here are lovely.

pairWith.why: the town end of the same beach
another big dune-backed beach to the north
a small free museum in Perranporth

tips: Wander into the dunes (on the paths) to look for the site of St Piran’s Oratory.
